Embla's demo scope includes scientific schematics: channel timelines, annotated
waveforms, spectra, state symbols, and arrows linking physical concepts. These
examples use editable Plotly traces, shapes, and labels.

```{=html}
<style>
#quarto-document-content { max-width: none; width: 100%; }
.cell-output-display { overflow-x: auto; max-width: 100%; }
.cell-output-display .js-plotly-plot { min-width: 800px; }
</style>
```

```{python}
#| include: false
from schematics import control_sequence, photon_diagram
from review import display_figure, for_renderings
def show_diagram(fig):
    fig.update_layout(width=800, autosize=False)
    display_figure(fig, config={"displayModeBar": False, "responsive": False})
```

## Control timeline

Five channels show two swaps, a reset, and phase compensation. Block positions
and gaps are schematic; the 40 ns text labels an example pulse only. Horizontal
scroll preserves readable labels on narrow screens.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
for_renderings(lambda mode: show_diagram(control_sequence(dark=mode == "dark")))
```

## Wave packet and receiver

A spectrum, a rising temporal envelope, a propagation path, and a two-level
receiver share one diagram. Λ and Γ are concept labels, not fitted parameters.
No device measurement or quantitative spectrum–envelope equivalence is claimed.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
for_renderings(lambda mode: show_diagram(photon_diagram(dark=mode == "dark")))
```

See [3D](three-d.qmd) for Bloch sphere animations and [Lines](lines.qmd) for
